title: Lean-STaR: Learning to Interleave Thinking and Proving
abstract: Lean-STaR is a framework for training language models to produce informal thoughts prior to each step of a proof, boosting the model's theorem-proving capabilities. By generating synthetic thoughts and fine-tuning the model on correct proofs, Lean-STaR achieves state-of-the-art results on formal theorem proving benchmarks.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a complex math problem. You don't just write down the solution - you think through each step, using informal reasoning to guide your formal calculations. Lean-STaR applies this same idea to automated theorem proving, using chain-of-thought rationales to improve the performance of language models.

By generating synthetic thoughts and fine-tuning the model on correct proofs, Lean-STaR achieves state-of-the-art results on formal theorem proving benchmarks.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
Lean-STaR works by first generating synthetic thoughts using a powerful language model, then fine-tuning the model on these thoughts and the corresponding formal proofs. This process is repeated using expert iteration, where the model is fine-tuned on the correct proofs it samples and verifies using the Lean solver.

The result is a model that can generate informal thoughts and formal proofs, improving its overall theorem-proving performance.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
Lean-STaR achieves state-of-the-art results on the miniF2F-test benchmark, with a pass rate of 46.3% using the InternLM2-plus-7b model. This is a significant improvement over the baseline model, which achieves a pass rate of 43.4%.

The results demonstrate the effectiveness of Lean-STaR in improving the theorem-proving capabilities of language models.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
The ability to generate informal thoughts and formal proofs has significant implications for automated theorem proving. By improving the performance of language models, Lean-STaR can help discover new mathematical insights and prove complex theorems.

The approach also has potential applications in education and research, where it can be used to generate explanations and proofs for mathematical concepts.

config.title: The Intersection of Thoughts and Proofs

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
Lean-STaR introduces several key innovations, including the use of synthetic thoughts and expert iteration to improve the performance of language models. The approach also demonstrates the effectiveness of combining informal and formal reasoning in automated theorem proving.

The results have significant implications for the development of more advanced theorem-proving systems.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
To try Lean-STaR yourself, you can use the InternLM2-plus-7b model and fine-tune it on the miniF2F-test benchmark. You can also experiment with different models and benchmarks to see the effectiveness of Lean-STaR in improving theorem-proving performance.

The code and data are available online, and we encourage you to try out Lean-STaR and see the results for yourself.
